# Lesson 2 — choosing by addressee, relationship and setting There is no single Japanese line that means "I love you". The same feeling is carried by different lines depending on who is listening, how close you are, and where you are standing. The English word stays fixed; the Japanese line moves. ## The four lines in this lesson | Relationship | Setting | Line | Romaji | English | |---|---|---|---|---| | friend | casual, after an outing | 好きだよ | suki da yo | I like you | | someone you respect but are not close to | private, first confession

Lesson 2 — choosing by addressee, relationship and setting
There is no single Japanese line that means "I love you". The same feeling is carried by
different lines depending on who is listening, how close you are, and where you are standing.
The English word stays fixed; the Japanese line moves.
The four lines in this lesson
Relationship
	
Setting
	
Line
	
Romaji
	
English
friend	casual, after an outing	好きだよ	suki da yo	I like you
someone you respect but are not close to	private, first confession	好きです	suki desu	I like you (polite)
close partner	everyday, warm	大好き	daisuki	I really like you
long-term partner	private
